newsitem.title: USA: Talks resume in drive to save California redwoods.
newsitem.headline: Talks resume in drive to save California redwoods.

text.p: One day before a loggers' deadline, talks resumed Thursday in Sen. Dianne Feinstein's office in an effort to prevent the felling of thousands of acres of ancient northern California redwoods.

The California Democrat met with Deputy Interior Secretary John Garamendi, California State Resources Secretary Doug Wheeler and Charles Hurwitz, the Texas financier who heads MAXXAM Inc., which owns the land.

Garamendi and Wheeler also met Wednesday afternoon in Sacramento with some of the people involved. Other meetings were held last week. Spokesmen for Garamendi and Feinstein said they expected the meeting Thursday to last hours and possibly run into the night.

Pacific Lumber Co., a unit of MAXXAM, agreed to delay the start of logging for two weeks in the virgin 3,000-acre (1,200-hectare) Headwaters area, a small part of the nearly 200,000 acres (81,000 hectares) owned by the company.

The deadline is Friday and logging could begin Monday without an agreement on the nation's largest privately held tract of redwoods. Environmentalists have sought to have 60,000 acres (24,000 hectares) protected, saying the area is an ecosystem necessary to preserve endangered fish and birds.
But the negotiations centre on the Headwaters area, a buffer zone of 1,500 acres (600 hectares) and about 1,800 to 3,000 acres (700-1,200 hectares) included in five other virgin forest parcels.
The struggle between environmentalists and the company sparked one of the largest one-day mass arrests ever in California this month when 897 people were arrested.
